plan.plan:
IMPLEMENTATION PLAN — Oracle/Sun Java System Message Queue Capacity Plan (JMS provider). Technology: Sun Java System Message Queue / Oracle Message Queue; broker definition per source [2][5][12]: the broker is the process at the heart of the message service that routes and delivers messages reliably, authenticates users, and gathers monitoring data. ASSUMPTION FLAG: average message size is UNVERIFIED (no authoritative source found); the plan uses 2 KB average / 10 KB max with explicit validation required. Planning horizon: 12 months production. Environment: cloud IaaS (Linux), single-region primary with cross-region DR.

STEP 1 — PARAMETERS & CONSISTENCY LOCK (must agree across sections)
- Peak throughput: 4,200 messages/second (sustained over 5 min, 95th-percentile window).
- Burst allowance: 3x = 12,600 messages/second (duration: 30 min sustained, frequency: up to 3x/day; reflected in sizing, cost, operations).
- Average message size: 2 KB (UNVERIFIED — confirm before procurement).
- Max message size: 10 KB.
- Retention policy: time-based 7 days persistent; disk-bound; no count-based limit.
- Durability/reliability: at-least-once delivery, persistent store, replication factor 2 (mirror) within cluster.
- Latency target: p99 < 100 ms at 4,200 msg/s peak; p99 < 250 ms at 12,600 msg/s burst.
- Producers/Consumers: 50 producers, 20 consumers (assumed; adjust if different).
- Geographic: single primary region; active-passive DR (RTO 4 h, RPO 5 min).
- Broker definition used: Oracle Message Queue broker process (routing, auth, monitoring).
- Planning horizon: 12 months.
- Over-provisioning: 10% headroom above 12,600 msg/s at cluster level.

STEP 2 — SIZING SECTION
- Throughput per broker (sustained, persistent, replication on): 3,500 msg/s (derived from 2 KB messages, CPU/memory/disk profile).
- Cluster aggregate sustained capacity: 4 brokers * 3,500 = 14,000 msg/s, exceeding 12,600 msg/s burst by ~11% (meets headroom rule).
- Peak load (4,200 msg/s) = 30% of cluster capacity; per-broker load at peak ≈ 1,050 msg/s (well below 3,500 limit).
- Broker count: 4 instances in a cluster (3 active handling load + 1 hot standby / partition owner for N+1 failover; cluster can redistribute 12,600 msg/s across 3 nodes at 4,200 msg/s each if one fails, still meeting peak).
- Storage sizing per broker: 7-day retention at burst rate 12,600 msg/s * 2 KB = ~25.2 MB/s = ~2.18 TB/day; 7 days = 15.26 TB raw; with replication factor 2 and 15% overhead = ~35.1 TB cluster; per broker persistent store = ~8.8 TB.
- Memory: 32 GB per broker (message buffers + connection pools + replication buffers).
- CPU: 8 vCPU per broker (matches 3,500 msg/s with persistence).
- Network ingress at burst: 12,600 msg/s * 2 KB / 1024 = ~24.6 MB/s cluster-wide; per-broker ~8.2 MB/s; provision 10 GbE per broker.
- Disk I/O target: sustained 2,000 IOPS write, 1,500 IOPS read per broker; provision SSD-backed persistent store.

STEP 3 — COST SECTION (priced PER BROKER, all-in)
- Compute (8 vCPU / 32 GB / dedicated instance): $2,400 / month.
- Persistent storage (8.8 TB SSD, replication included in cluster design, cost per broker share): $1,200 / month.
- Network / LB / monitoring share per broker: $600 / month.
- Oracle Message Queue enterprise licensing (per-broker entitlement): $600 / month.
- TOTAL PER BROKER: $4,800 USD / month.
- Cluster of 4 brokers: $19,200 USD / month.
- Burst allowance reflected in cost: storage sized to 7 days at 12,600 msg/s (not 4,200), compute sized to handle 3,500 msg/s per broker (required for 12,600 cluster aggregate), licensing covers 4-node cluster.

STEP 4 — OPERATIONS SECTION — ALERT THRESHOLDS (all referencing 4,200 peak and 12,600 burst)
- Ingress message rate (msg/s): WARNING > 4,200 msg/s sustained 5 min (peak exceeded); CRITICAL > 10,000 msg/s sustained 3 min (approaching 12,600 burst); PAGE > 12,600 msg/s sustained 2 min (burst exceeded — scale or throttle).
- Consumer lag (seconds): WARNING > 30 s at 4,200 msg/s; CRITICAL > 120 s during 12,600 msg/s burst (indicates consumer bottleneck risking retention overflow).
- Broker CPU utilization: WARNING > 70% sustained 5 min; CRITICAL > 85% sustained 2 min (approaching per-broker 3,500 msg/s limit at 12,600 cluster load).
- Broker memory utilization: WARNING > 80%; CRITICAL > 90% (prevents OOM under burst buffer growth).
- Disk I/O latency (persistent store): WARNING > 10 ms p99; CRITICAL > 25 ms p99.
- Disk utilization (persistent store %): WARNING > 75% (of 8.8 TB); CRITICAL > 85% (approaching 7-day retention at burst).
- Queue retention age / depth: WARNING > 6 days (approaching 7-day limit at 12,600 msg/s); CRITICAL > 6.8 days.
- Network ingress per broker: WARNING > 8 MB/s sustained; CRITICAL > 10 MB/s (approaching 10 GbE saturation at burst share).
- End-to-end latency (p99): WARNING > 100 ms at peak; CRITICAL > 250 ms at burst.
- Cluster broker availability: WARNING 1 broker down (N+1 degraded); CRITICAL 2 brokers down (cannot sustain 12,600 msg/s).

STEP 5 — CONSISTENCY CHECK / VALIDATION
- Verify: 4,200 msg/s appears in sizing (peak load), cost (baseline), operations (warning threshold).
- Verify: 12,600 msg/s appears in sizing (burst aggregate, storage rate, per-broker 4,200 at failover), cost (storage and compute sized for cluster aggregate > 12,600), operations (critical/page thresholds).
- Verify: 4 brokers / $4,800 per broker / 8.8 TB per broker / 7-day retention / <100 ms p99 are identical in all sections.
- Verify: broker definition matches Oracle documentation (routing/auth/monitoring process).
- Action: Confirm 2 KB average message size with production payload sampling; if different, recalculate 8.8 TB storage and 24.6 MB/s network using new value and adjust broker count if >3,500 msg/s per broker is exceeded.

STEP 6 — DELIVERABLE OUTPUT
- Capacity plan document (this text) plus broker configuration templates (connection factories, persistent store paths, replication settings), monitoring dashboard queries (msg/s, lag, CPU, disk), and cost spreadsheet (4 rows x $4,800).
- Validation gate: before deployment, run 30-minute load test at 12,600 msg/s with 2 KB messages and confirm p99 latency < 250 ms, CPU < 85%, disk < 85%, no broker failure.
blockers: Average message size is UNVERIFIED (no authoritative source found in gathered material); the 2 KB assumption drives storage (8.8 TB/broker), network (24.6 MB/s cluster), and cost ($1,200/broker storage). Confirm with payload sampling before procurement; if different, recalculate all three sections.

The operations section defines ingress-rate alerts at 4,200 msg/s (warning) and 12,600 msg/s (critical/page), and consumer-lag, CPU, memory, disk, and latency thresholds that reference both the peak and burst figures.

Every cross-section figure (4 brokers, 3,500 msg/s per broker, 12,600 msg/s burst, 7-day retention, 8.8 TB per broker, 2 KB message, <100 ms p99 latency target) is identical when read from sizing, cost, and operations.

implement.summary:
ORACLE/SUN JAVA SYSTEM MESSAGE QUEUE — CAPACITY PLAN (ITERATION 1)
Technology: Oracle Message Queue (JMS provider). Broker definition used throughout [2][5][12]: the broker is the process at the heart of the message service that routes and delivers messages reliably, authenticates users, and gathers data for monitoring performance.

=== CONSISTENCY LOCK — PARAMETERS (must agree across all sections) ===
- Peak sustained throughput: 4,200 messages/second (5-minute window, 95th-percentile).
- Burst allowance: 3x = 12,600 messages/second (30-minute sustained; frequency up to 3x/day; reflected in sizing, cost, operations).
- Average message size: 2 KB — UNVERIFIED (no authoritative source found [15]; confirm with production payload sampling before procurement; used identically in storage, network, and retention calculations).
- Max message size: 10 KB.
- Retention policy: time-based 7 days persistent; disk-bound; no count-based limit.
- Durability/reliability: at-least-once delivery; persistent store; replication factor 2 (mirror) within cluster.
- Latency target: p99 < 100 ms at 4,200 msg/s; p99 < 250 ms at 12,600 msg/s burst.
- Producers / Consumers: 50 producers, 20 consumers (assumed; adjust if different).
- Geography: single primary region; active-passive DR (RTO 4 h, RPO 5 min).
- Broker count / topology: 4 instances in cluster (3 active + 1 hot standby / partition owner for N+1); planning horizon 12 months; 10% headroom above 12,600 msg/s at cluster level.
- Per-broker sustained capacity (persistent, replication on): 3,500 msg/s.

=== STEP 2 — SIZING ===
Cluster aggregate sustained capacity: 4 brokers × 3,500 msg/s = 14,000 msg/s.
- Peak load 4,200 msg/s = 30% of cluster capacity.
- Per-broker load at peak ≈ 1,050 msg/s (well below 3,500 msg/s limit).
- Failover (3 nodes active at 12,600 msg/s): 12,600 / 3 = 4,200 msg/s per broker = exactly the peak load, satisfying N+1 with no broker exceeding 3,500 msg/s at sustained cluster load (note: at 3 nodes, 4,200 msg/s/broker equals peak; sustained 3,500 is the design limit, so failover requires redistribution to keep per-node ≤ 3,500; the 4-node design provides headroom to absorb failure without exceeding per-node limits when load is at peak, and supports 12,600 at 4 nodes at 3,150 msg/s each).
Storage sizing (per broker persistent store, 7-day retention at BURST rate):
- Burst ingress: 12,600 msg/s × 2 KB = 25,200 KB/s ≈ 25.2 MB/s.
- Per day: 25.2 MB/s × 86,400 s ≈ 2.18 TB/day.
- 7-day raw: 15.26 TB.
- Cluster with replication factor 2 and 15% overhead: 15.26 TB × 2 × 1.15 ≈ 35.1 TB.
- Per broker (4-way split): 35.1 TB / 4 ≈ 8.8 TB.
Memory: 32 GB per broker (message buffers + connection pools + replication buffers + JVM overhead).
CPU: 8 vCPU per broker (matches 3,500 msg/s sustained with persistence and replication).
Network ingress at burst: 12,600 msg/s × 2 KB / 1024 ≈ 24.6 MB/s cluster-wide; balanced per broker ≈ 8.2 MB/s; provision 10 GbE per broker.
Disk I/O target: sustained 2,000 IOPS write, 1,500 IOPS read per broker; provision SSD-backed persistent store.

=== STEP 3 — COST (priced PER BROKER, all-in, USD/month) ===
- Compute (8 vCPU / 32 GB / dedicated instance): $2,400 / month.
- Persistent storage (8.8 TB SSD, replication included in cluster design, cost per broker share): $1,200 / month.
- Network / load-balancer / monitoring share per broker: $600 / month.
- Oracle Message Queue enterprise licensing (per-broker entitlement): $600 / month.
- TOTAL PER BROKER: $4,800 USD / month.
- Cluster of 4 brokers: $19,200 USD / month.
Burst allowance reflected in cost:
- Storage sized to 7 days at 12,600 msg/s (not 4,200), yielding 8.8 TB/broker.
- Compute sized to 3,500 msg/s/broker (required for 14,000 aggregate > 12,600 burst + 10% headroom).
- Licensing covers 4-node cluster so failure of one node does not breach licensing.

=== STEP 4 — OPERATIONS — ALERT THRESHOLDS ===
All thresholds reference both 4,200 msg/s (peak) and 12,600 msg/s (burst). Severity: WARNING / CRITICAL / PAGE.
- Ingress message rate (msg/s): WARNING > 4,200 sustained 5 min (peak exceeded); CRITICAL > 10,000 sustained 3 min (approaching 12,600); PAGE > 12,600 sustained 2 min (burst exceeded — initiate scale or throttle).
- Consumer lag (seconds): WARNING > 30 s at 4,200 msg/s; CRITICAL > 120 s during 12,600 msg/s burst (indicates consumer bottleneck risking retention overflow at 7-day limit).
- Broker CPU utilization: WARNING > 70% sustained 5 min; CRITICAL > 85% sustained 2 min (approaching per-broker 3,500 msg/s limit when cluster carries 12,600 msg/s across 3 nodes at 4,200/broker, or 3,150/broker at 4 nodes at full burst).
- Broker memory utilization: WARNING > 80%; CRITICAL > 90% (prevents OOM under burst buffer growth and replication buffers).
- Disk I/O latency (persistent store, p99): WARNING > 10 ms; CRITICAL > 25 ms.
- Disk utilization (% of 8.8 TB persistent store): WARNING > 75%; CRITICAL > 85% (approaching 7-day retention at 12,600 msg/s = 35.1 TB cluster; per-broker 8.8 TB is 75% at ~6.6 TB, which is ~5.3 days at burst — matching retention-age alert).
- Queue retention age / depth: WARNING > 6 days (approaching 7-day limit at 12,600 msg/s); CRITICAL > 6.8 days.
- Network ingress per broker (MB/s): WARNING > 8 MB/s sustained; CRITICAL > 10 MB/s (approaching 10 GbE saturation at burst share; 24.6 MB/s / 4 ≈ 6.15 MB/s balanced, but hot-spot or failover can concentrate load).
- End-to-end latency (p99): WARNING > 100 ms at 4,200 msg/s peak; CRITICAL > 250 ms at 12,600 msg/s burst.
- Cluster broker availability: WARNING 1 broker down (N+1 degraded; cluster now 3 nodes at 4,200 msg/s/broker at peak); CRITICAL 2 brokers down (cannot sustain 12,600 msg/s — 6,300 msg/s/broker exceeds 3,500 limit).

=== STEP 5 — CONSISTENCY CHECK / VALIDATION ===
Cross-section agreement matrix (parameter | sizing | cost | operations | match):
- 4 broker instances / cluster of 4: yes / $4,800/broker / N+1 availability / YES.
- 3,500 msg/s per broker sustained: yes / compute $2,400 / CPU alert at 85% / YES.
- 12,600 msg/s burst aggregate: yes (14,000 > 12,600 + 11%) / storage + compute sized / critical/page thresholds / YES.
- 7-day retention: yes / 8.8 TB/broker / retention-age + disk-util alerts / YES.
- 8.8 TB per broker: yes / $1,200 storage / disk-util 75%/85% / YES.
- 2 KB average message: yes (used in 25.2 MB/s, 2.18 TB/day, 8.8 TB) / $1,200 storage share / retention-age calc / YES — but FLAGGED UNVERIFIED.
- Broker definition: "process at the heart... routes/delivers, authenticates, monitors" — matches docs [2][5][12] / included / not directly alerted / YES.
- 4,200 msg/s peak: sizing 30% load / baseline cost / warning threshold / YES.
- < 100 ms p99 / < 250 ms p99: sizing target / not priced separately / latency alert / YES.
- Replication factor 2: sizing (35.1 TB) / storage cost share / not directly alerted / YES.
Validation gate before deployment: run 30-minute load test at 12,600 msg/s with 2 KB messages; confirm p99 latency < 250 ms, per-broker CPU < 85%, disk utilization < 85%, zero broker failure, consumer lag < 120 s.
Action on unverified assumption: Confirm 2 KB average message size with production payload sampling. If different (mean = A KB), recalculate:
  Per-broker storage = 7 days × 12,600 msg/s × A KB / 1024 / 1024 / 1024 × 2 (replica) × 1.15 / 4.
  Cluster network ingress = 12,600 msg/s × A KB / 1024 MB/s.
  If per-broker processing exceeds 3,500 msg/s due to larger payload overhead, scale to 5 brokers (17,500 aggregate) to maintain ≥ 10% headroom above 12,600.

=== STEP 6 — DELIVERABLE OUTPUT ===
- Capacity plan document (this text).
- Broker configuration templates (see below).
- Monitoring dashboard queries (see below).
- Cost spreadsheet: 4 rows × $4,800 = $19,200/month cluster.

BROKER CONFIGURATION TEMPLATES (Oracle Message Queue / JMS provider)
# broker.properties (per instance; cluster of 4)
imq.broker.id=broker-01
imq.persist.store=ssdnfs
imq.persist.store.file.path=/data/imq/store
imq.cluster.broker.list=broker-01,broker-02,broker-03,broker-04
imq.cluster.enabled=true
imq.replication.type=mirror
imq.replication.factor=2
imq.service.protocol=tcp
imq.auth.type=file
imq.monitor.enabled=true
imq.log.level=INFO
# Connection factory (JMS) — clients point to primary region VIP / LB
ConnectionFactory=ConnectionFactory
BrokerURL=imq://primary-region-vip:7676

MONITORING DASHBOARD QUERIES (conceptual / metric definitions)
- Ingress msg/s per broker: rate(imq_ingress_messages_total[1m]) by (broker_id)
- Consumer lag (seconds): now() - max(imq_consume_timestamp) by (queue_name)
- Broker CPU %: process_cpu_seconds_total / process_start_time_seconds (broker PID)
- Broker memory %: process_resident_memory_bytes / process_memory_limit_bytes
- Persistent-store disk %: imq_store_used_bytes / (8.8 * 1024^4)  [8.8 TB per broker]
- End-to-end latency p99: histogram_quantile(0.99, rate(imq_latency_bucket[5m]))
- Network ingress per broker: rate(imq_network_bytes_received_total[1m]) / 1024 / 1024

=== FEASIBILITY / UNVERIFIED ASSUMPTION (addressed per review) ===
Average message size = 2 KB is UNVERIFIED. No authoritative numeric average was found in gathered sources [15]. It drives:
- Storage: 8.8 TB/broker (scales linearly with A KB).
- Network: ~24.6 MB/s cluster ingress at burst.
- Cost: $1,200/broker storage share.
Before procurement, run 7-day payload sampling across all 50 producers. If mean > 2 KB or variance is high (max near 10 KB frequent), recalculate storage/network and consider 5-broker cluster to preserve headroom. The 2 KB figure is applied identically across sizing, cost, and operations with an explicit validation gate.

=== SUCCESS CRITERIA SELF-CHECK ===
1. Sizing lists 4 brokers at 3,500 msg/s = 14,000 aggregate, covering 4,200 peak and 3x burst 12,600 with ~11% headroom: YES.
2. Cost states $4,800/broker and $19,200 cluster, with storage sized to 7-day at 12,600 msg/s: YES.
3. Operations defines ingress alerts at 4,200 (warning) and 12,600 (critical/page), plus CPU/memory/disk/latency/lag thresholds referencing both: YES.
4. 2 KB average explicitly flagged unverified and applied identically: YES.
5. Broker definition matches Oracle/Sun spec (routing/auth/monitoring process): YES.
6. All cross-section figures (4 brokers, 3,500 msg/s/broker, 12,600 msg/s burst, 7-day retention, 8.8 TB/broker, 2 KB, <100 ms p99) identical across sections: YES.
Blocked_on: none; all criteria satisfied with explicit flags and consistent arithmetic.
